title: Declare per-model SLO currency and staged failover escrow for session-affine conversational routes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Many of our conversational customers use session-affine model endpoints where KV cache state and token continuity materially affect both latency and quality. Existing SLO work focuses on route-level availability and latency, but does not encode tokenized cost or session affinity. During regional capacity pressure we've observed poor failover behavior for session-affine routes: either full session eviction (bad UX) or excessive burn on degraded variants (cost and quality regressions).

Problem statement:
- We need a per-model SLO declaration that treats error budget as a first-class currency expressed in token-equivalents, not only requests or time.
- We must define a staged failover "escrow" that permits short-term borrowing of error budget during regional failover without catastrophic cross-region depletion.
- Circuit breaker handoff semantics should preserve session-affine warm state where possible and prefer graceful degradation (reduce quality) over hard evictions.

Proposal summary:
1) SLI definitions (model-level, session-affine aware):
   - Latency SLI: P95 inference latency (tail measured server-side, excluding network) per 30d window. Goal: P95 < 200ms for low-latency tier; non-low-latency tiers have tier-specific thresholds declared in model profile.
   - Availability SLI: Successful response fraction (2xx + structured error-handled responses) per 30d window. Goal: 99.9% for production-tier models.
   - Quality SLI (response quality signal): Regression rate on closed prompt-sets (synthetic prompts & canonical evaluations) per 7d window. Goal: regression rate < 1.0% relative to pinned baseline.
   - Session-coherency SLI: Fraction of multi-turn sessions with uninterrupted KV cache continuity (no forced rewarm/eviction) for sessions < 60m. Goal: 98% continuity.

2) Error-budget currency and accounting:
   - Define 1 unit of error-budget = 1 effective token (user tokens + model tokens weighted by model-cost-profile).
   - Token burn per request = (user_tokens + model_tokens) * model_weight; model_weight is derived from GPU/quantization profile in the model catalog.
   - Monthly error budget allocated per model = function(traffic, tier, SLOs). Example: model-m-prod receives 10M token-units/month.
   - Error budget burn attributable to quality regressions: when synthetic-eval regression fires, a proportional token deduction is applied based on number of affected sessions in lookback window.

3) Staged failover escrow (cross-region borrowing):
   - Each model has Regional Buckets (RB) and a Central Escrow (CE). RB_i replenishes from CE only under declared failover conditions.
   - Emergency borrow cap: RB can borrow up to 15% of CE for up to 6 hours with mandatory cooldown and reconciliation.
   - Automatic reconciliation: borrowed units are repaid from future RB allocations over the subsequent 7-day window (linear repayment) to avoid long-term imbalance.
   - Borrowing is gated by: current burn rate, predicted capacity shortage (from autoscaler signals), and customer-impact priority.

4) Circuit breaker and handoff semantics for session-affine routes:
   - Thresholds: circuit opens on sustained token-burn-per-second above X or on P99 latency spike > Y for 5m window (configurable per model).
   - Handoff behavior when circuit trips:
       a) Prefer warm-variant fallback that preserves KV cache continuity if available in target region/variant.
       b) If only cold fallback exists, enter progressive-degradation: reduce max_output_tokens and enable sampling/quantization friendly variant to reduce per-token cost.
       c) Mark session as "degraded" and attach metadata to response so client can show graceful-degradation UX.
   - Hysteresis: minimum closed duration 10m; exponential backoff on retries.

5) Load-shedding priority matrix:
   - Priority order for eviction/load-shedding: system-critical health checks > enterprise SLA pinned sessions > paid low-latency tier > standard sessions > best-effort background jobs.
   - For session-affine routes, when eviction unavoidable: shrink session retention window (KV idle TTL) before evicting active sessions to preserve continuity for recently active users.

Telemetry and signals:
- New metrics to emit per model+region: token_burn/sec, token_burn/30d, session_continuity_rate, synthetic_regression_rate, escrow_borrowed_units, escrow_repayment_rate.
- Alerts:
  * Escrow borrow > 75% of CE -> Sev2 page and slack channel notify with suggested mitigation steps.
  * token_burn/sec sustained > planned capacity curve (5m) -> auto throttle/scale recommendation and Sev1 if sustained > 15m.
  * session_continuity_rate drop > 2% within 1h -> automatic revert to warm fallback and postmortem trigger.

Simulations and early results:
- Simulated a regional outage for model-m-prod (80% capacity loss in us-east) and allowed RB to borrow 10% of CE: predicted 4h runway with progressive-degradation policy, 12% quality drop on degraded responses but 87% session continuity retained vs 23% with naive eviction.
- Cost estimate: expected additional token burn during borrow window ~ +9% across org; repayment redistributes ~1.5% of future monthly budget for next 7 days.

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
- SLO manifest spec published in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/display/ENG/Session-Affine+SLO+Currency (draft link).
- Telemetry emitted and visible in console dashboard for one model canary (model-m-canary): token_burn/sec, escrow_borrowed_units, session_continuity_rate.
- Failover escrow simulation executed in staging with canary traffic and results documented.
- Circuit breaker config implemented in runtime-config repo and landed behind runtime feature-flag. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1846
- Runbook updated with step-by-step manual overrides and escalation path.

Open questions / trade-offs discussed:
- Pricing vs SLO currency: should token-units translate directly to billing signals? Trade-off between billing complexity and operational clarity. Proposal: keep internal currency decoupled from billing for now.
- Repayment policy fairness when CE is scarce: use proportional repayment weighted by regional traffic rather than first-come-first-served to avoid starvation.
- Quality SLI measurement for multilingual models where synthetic promptsets have limited coverage; we propose per-language pinning and conservative thresholds.

Next steps and owners:

- Maya (infra): add telemetry counters to serving runtime and wire to metrics exporter (ETA 2025-02-25).
- Clara (product): review and approve staged failover escrow policy with customer success for enterprise contracts (ETA 2025-02-28).
- Eng QA: run failure-mode simulation in staging (ETA 2025-02-27).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: CE depletion and cascading cross-region failures. Mitigation: hard global cap on concurrent borrow = 30% of CE across all models and enforced cooldown with automated repayment.
- Risk: telemetry cost and cardinality spike. Mitigation: roll out to canaries with cardinality limits and aggregated rollups before org-wide activation.

If there are no objections, I'll draft the Confluence SLO manifest page and request a brief ops-runbook review session next week to align on manual overrides.
